title: fix: keep non-ASCII and binary bytes intact in the computer shell
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
Agents writing files with heredocs or `base64 -d` on the computer got garbled text (`café` → `cafÃ©`) in their files and pushed commits. Reported in #15075, #15310 and #15419. Addresses #15519.

- Fix: patch `@cloudflare/computer` 0.3's bundled shell adapter to honour the `"binary"` encoding just-bash passes on writes and appends.
- Fix: decode UTF-8 in just-bash's `read` and `mapfile`, which stored raw bytes in variables, so `echo "$line"` encoded them again.
- Adds byte-level tests: stdin, heredoc, printf, tee, `<` redirect, `>>` append, `base64 -d`, a git commit of the result, and `read`/`mapfile` from stdin, pipes and here-strings.
- Pass `stdin` through `runtime.exec` again; the `/tmp` file workaround from #14741 is no longer needed.
- Bump the shell loader revision so cached shell isolates pick up the new code.

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| heredoc, `tee` | 33 bytes | 23 |
| `cat < f > g` | 53 bytes | 23 |
| `base64 -d` (10-byte PNG header) | 12 bytes | 10 |
| `read`/`mapfile` then `echo` | 33 bytes | 23 |

The patches throw at startup if they stop applying. Remove them once upstream honours the encoding.

Staging (`pollinations-computer-mcp-staging` 8d75781d, via staging gen): all seven write paths store the exact bytes, and jq, curl, xan and `/tmp` cleanup still work.

Still broken (upstream):
- `$(…)` command substitution of non-ASCII bytes, and raw bytes piped into the bundled `jq`; `jq --arg` is unsupported.
- `git show HEAD:<binary>` prints binary bytes as U+FFFD. Stored blobs and `git checkout` are correct.

gist.headline: The bytes made it home
gist.blurb: voodoohop fixed the computer shell’s habit of turning `café` into `cafÃ©`. Heredocs, decoded files, and git commits can now keep the bytes they were given.
gist.summary: voodoohop patched the computer-mcp shell’s binary writes and UTF-8 handling in `read` and `mapfile`, so heredocs, `base64 -d`, redirects, and commits preserve their original bytes.
gist.impact: Agents using the computer shell can write non-ASCII text and binary files without those bytes changing on the way to disk or into a git commit.
